Application Materials.content:
Documents and information you’ll need:
- a copy of your degree certificate and transcript, or a partial transcript if you’re still studying
- contact details for two academic references
- a personal statement
- an up-to-date CV
- your approved English Language test* (if applicable)
- a letter of sponsorship, if you need one.
* Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Interview Requirements.content: Interviews do not form part of the Business School’s standard admissions process. However, in some cases, an applicant may be invited for an interview if it will help inform whether an offer should be made.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons).** Core quantitative skills and willingness to engage with quantitative materials are essential.
- International equivalents: the University accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-equivalents-2).
- For applicants from China: accepted postgraduate qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school; applicants should check that their institution is accepted and that they meet the entry requirements before applying.
- For applicants from China, where a **2.1** is required: **70%-85%, depending on your institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall**, with no less than **6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course. Options mentioned include [Language for Business (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k022/language-for-business-6-weeks- "Language for Marketing 6 weeks"), [Language for Business (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k023/language-for-business-10-weeks- "Language for Business: Marketing (10 weeks)"), [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).
Documents and information needed include “your approved English Language test* (if applicable).” Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/english-language-requirements-2) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.

Program Overview.content:
Start date: 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
Business Analytics and Decision Sciences MSc is designed to develop expertise in data analysis and the psychology of how people make decisions, so students can transform data into meaningful business action. The course combines theoretical concepts with practical application, developing decision-oriented analytical skills that managers need. Students learn how to translate data, such as customer reviews, sales figures and cost-over-time, into actionable insights that have a positive impact on organisational effectiveness.
The course builds knowledge and understanding of how business analytics can provide evidence to support management decision making. Using different evidence-based approaches to make effective decisions, students develop quantitative analysis skills and learn advanced analytical techniques such as forecasting, predictive modelling, clustering and optimisation, while applying decision-making skills to real-life business and management scenarios. Students also gain an understanding of research methods and consultancy. A range of optional modules allows students to gain specialist knowledge that suits their interests or career plans. The course culminates in a dissertation or project, enabling students to apply their learning to a topic of their choice with support from an academic supervisor.
- Taught by globally recognised experts: academics and business practitioners who teach the course are from the [Centre for Decision Research](https://cdr.leeds.ac.uk/about/) and are actively engaged in advising businesses, governments and international bodies.
- The curriculum is based on real business applications shaped by industry links, with opportunities to work with and learn from major names in business.
- Students can apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-study-tour-2), with company visits, guest lectures and networking events. Previous study tours have included Berlin, Frankfurt, Milan and Zurich.
- Students have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.
Leeds University Business School has triple accreditation from the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations), [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations), and [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations).
Students are taught through lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops, with independent learning supported by the Virtual Learning Environment. Teaching is delivered by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors, and may also include industry professionals with years of experience and trained postgraduate researchers. Assessment may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
Career paths for graduates include Business Analysts, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Data Hunters, Business Consultants, Analytics Consultants and Commercial Managers. Graduates have found employment as Credit Risk Manager at Lloyds Banking Group, Business Analyst at Transport for London, Business QA Manager at HSBC, Associate at PwC, Analyst at Deloitte, Data Hunter at Allianz Insurance, Consultant at EY, Senior Advisor Data Science at Dell Technologies, Accountant at Beijing Capital Airlines and Operational Researcher at the Home Office.
Key skills developed include business analytics using industry-standard tools such as R, Python and SQL; processes such as CRISP-DM and Agile; time-series forecasting and machine learning, including the application of artificial intelligence; decision making, including human bias and heuristics, risk communication and risk assessment; and business acumen for managing complex business situations.
Students engage with senior business leaders through the [Leaders in Residence](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/divisions-management/doc/leaders-residence) initiative. Past students have worked on industry-led projects with partners such as the Met Office, Britest, OPSS and Universal Music Group, and have been taught by experts in analytics and decision science from companies including Oakland, Amazon and PlayStation.
As a Masters student at Leeds, students can gain real-world industry experience through the Global Industry Programme, solving a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around studies, with opportunities to build professional networks, consultancy experience, teamwork across disciplines and employability prospects.
The programme is ranked [Top 60 in the world for Business Analytics, QS Business Masters Rankings 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics).

Curriculum.content:
Start date delivery type: **On campus**. Duration: **12 Months (Full time)**.
This course will build your knowledge and understanding of how business analytics can provide evidence to support management decision making. You’ll learn to use advanced analytical techniques, such as forecasting, predictive modelling, clustering and optimisation, while applying your decision-making skills to real-life business and management scenarios. You’ll also gain an understanding of research methods and consultancy. A range of optional modules allows you to gain specialist knowledge that suits your interests or career plans. The course culminates in a **dissertation or project**, enabling you to apply your learning to a topic of your choice.
[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Business Analytics and Decision Sciences MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-BS%2FBADS).
Year 1 compulsory modules:
| Module Name | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| Effective Decision Making | 15 |
| Advanced Management Decision Making | 15 |
| Business Analytics and Decision Science | 15 |
| Forecasting and Advanced Business Analytics | 15 |
| Evidence Based Consultancy | 15 |
| Research Methods and Dissertation | 60 |
| Quantitative Analysis | 15 |
Year 1 optional modules (selection of typical options shown below):
| Module Name | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| Supply Chain Analytics | 15 |
| Applied AI in Business | 15 |
| Managing Digital Information Projects | 15 |
| Techniques of Influence | 15 |
| Machine Learning in Practice | 15 |
| Creating Effective Data Visualisations | 15 |
| Digital Technologies for a Sustainable Future | 15 |
You’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. Assessment may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a **2-week online Global Industry Programme**. Benefits include: fully online and designed to fit around your studies; working on a time limited brief with a UK or international organisation; and working as part of a team across disciplines to tackle real business needs.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The following estimates are for a single student in 2025, based on the latest data available. They don’t include tuition fees. Actual amounts depend on accommodation type and availability, and lifestyle. All University accommodation costs include household bills and (except family accommodation) gym membership.
| Cost category | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Financial Aid.content: International Excellence Scholarships: **£3,000, £6,000 and £16,000 fee reduction scholarships** are available. These scholarships recognise and reward high academic achievement for students who have applied to study a taught Masters course starting in **2026**. Visit the [international Masters scholarships webpage](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-scholarships-funding/doc/masters-scholarships) to see what is available, check eligibility and find out how to apply.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: You do not need to have fulfilled all [entry requirements](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/entry-requirements-2) before applying. Provided your application satisfies all other entry requirements, a conditional offer may be made on the basis of a predicted result: for example, the final mark of your first degree or an English language test. You must provide your final results before an unconditional offer can be made. **The deadline for meeting your conditions is Friday 7 August 2026, 23:59 UK time.** This is to allow applicants who need a Student route visa time to be confirmed as unconditional, and to pay the tuition fee deposit or provide the sponsor evidence that is required for us to issue a CAS in support of the visa application.
